key_insight: APS-produced Fe79Zr6Si14Cu1 coatings remained predominantly crystalline despite rapid cooling, with a 90 mm spray distance providing the best overall property balance.
engineering_relevance: Spray-distance control helps balance hardness and wear resistance against porosity-driven corrosion vulnerability in these low-glass-forming-ability coatings.
method: Deposited Fe79Zr6Si14Cu1 coatings by atmospheric plasma spraying at different spray distances.
Characterized phase composition, lamellar microstructure, and porosity.
Evaluated hardness, wear resistance, and electrochemical behaviour.
evidence_signal: XRD detected α-Fe(Si) and Fe–Zr intermetallic phases but no amorphous fraction; porosity ranged from 2.2% to 4.9%, and increasing spray distance improved hardness and wear resistance while reducing corrosion resistance.
watch_item: The 90 mm condition was best only among the investigated settings; transfer to other APS systems requires validation of particle thermal history and coating defects.
paper_title: Phase Evolution and Structure–Property Relationships of Fe79Zr6Si14Cu1 Coatings with Low GFA Produced by Atmospheric Plasma Spraying
